name: color-field
title: Color field
summary: Lets people set one color as a field of a form: a text value they can read, type and paste, a sample of it beside the text, and a button that asks for a picker; it looks and measures like a text field.

anatomy.description: The Field: the label row with its glyph and its requirement mark, and the supporting row with the help and the error text. In a look whose input floats the label it draws no label row.
The color input, as the Field's one control: the box, the swatch, the value as text, the picker button, and the label that floats in the box in the looks that float one.

props.name: value
props.note: What the color field reports as its own is the value its color input holds, in that value's own form (CLF-43, CLI-16, CLI-21).

props.name: label
props.note: Names the color input. In a filled or outlined look the input draws it, floating in its box, and the Field draws no label row (FLD-25, CLI-15).

props.name: labelHidden
props.note: Hides the label wherever it would be drawn: the Field's row, or the input's floating label (FLD-25).

props.name: error
props.note: The Field puts its color input in the input's own error condition (FLD-8, CLI-9).

props.name: disabled
props.note: The Field disables its color input, the picker button with it (FLD-14, CLI-31); the color field is then left out of its form (CLF-44).

props.name: required
props.note: The Field exposes its color input as required (FLD-10, CLI-11).

props.name: invalidText
props.note: Shown by the Field, in its supporting row (FLD-28).

behavior.text: THE color field SHALL be a Field that frames one color input, and nothing else. It SHALL give label, labelHidden, supportingText, errorText, error, disabled, required, optional, requiredMark, requiredText and optionalText to its Field and variant, size, value, invalidText, picker and pickerLabel to its color input, each unchanged; SHALL hold the label-icon slot for its Field; and SHALL emit its color input's events as its own, each once. THE color field SHALL be as wide as the place it stands in, and its color input SHALL fill it: it is a block with no width of its own, as its Field is (FLD-1), around a control that fills the width it is given (CLI-44). Its value SHALL at every moment be the value its color input holds — a color in the value's own form, or the empty string (CLI-16) — and not the text the product set where the two differ (CLI-21). It SHALL draw no part of its own, hold no state of its own and have no token of its own: what it shows, how it behaves and what it exposes to assistive technology SHALL be exactly what that Field and that color input do when a product places the one in the other (FLD-1 to FLD-28; CLI-1 to CLI-44) — the label row and its requirement mark (FLD-2 to FLD-6), or the label that floats in the box with the Field's row left out (FLD-25, CLI-15, CLI-7); the supporting row, started at the value's text, after the swatch (FLD-7 to FLD-9, FLD-26, CLI-43); the name, the description and the states (FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14, CLI-11); and the entry error of a text that is not a color, shown in the Field's row (FLD-28, CLI-20).
behavior.verify: The twin test: every fixture of the color field has a twin, the Field's fixture color-<id>, a Field around a color input written by hand with the same values; on every platform that draws both, the two are the same picture and the same accessibility tree. A difference is a finding in a member or in the exchange between them (CLI-43), never a baseline to update. Unit: set value to "0F766E" and read it back as "#0f766e" with no event emitted.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has forms (the web) THE color field SHALL be the one control the form sees: it SHALL take name, submit its color input's value, reset to the value it was first given, restore it on navigation, report to the form's constraint validation exactly what its color input would report there (CLI-11, CLI-20), and be left out WHILE disabled is true or a disabled group of the form holds it; its color input and its Field SHALL take no part in the form themselves. WHEN the action key asks for the form's submission (CLI-19) the form asked SHALL be the color field's own.
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: a form with one color field submits one entry under the field's name, the color in its own form; reset and restore reach the color input; required true with an empty value reports valueMissing on the color field and focuses its input when the form reports it; a committed text that is not a color reports badInput; Enter in the input presses the form's default button (BTN-30).

behavior.text: WHEN the color field is given focus — by the product, by a press on any part of it that FLD-12 or CLI-24 gives to the input, or by a form that reports its validity — THE color field SHALL pass the focus to the input of its color input, never to the picker button, and SHALL add no stop to the focus order: the stops inside it are its color input's, in that input's order (the input, then the picker button while it is shown, CLI-13). WHILE focus is anywhere inside it, the picker button included, THE color field SHALL count as focused for its Field, whose rows take their focused colors (FLD-13); the box takes its own only WHILE its input has focus (CLI-22). WHEN a picker the color input presented closes, focus SHALL be on the picker button (CLI-29), inside the color field.

IF the color field is placed in a Field THE color field SHALL in debug builds report that it is a field already and that the bare control is the color input, and both SHALL still render (FLD-15). WHILE it stands in a field group THE color field SHALL follow that group's disabled, through its own Field, and take nothing else from the group (FGR-20).

THE color field SHALL have no words of its own and SHALL read none: requiredText and optionalText are read by its Field (FLD-24), each from the instance's prop and then from the product's words; invalidText and pickerLabel are the instance's alone and are given to its color input as they are (CLI-42).

keyboard.action: The color input's (its accessibility block; CLI-13, CLI-19, CLI-28). The color field handles no key and adds no focus stop (CLF-45).

accessibility.labeling: The color field adds nothing to what its members expose and coordinates nothing: the Field gives the color input its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14), and the color input carries them on its own element (CLI-11). Assistive technology meets one text box named by label whose value is the color as text, and, while picker is true, one button named by pickerLabel — exactly as it meets a Field around a color input written by hand.
notes: One level down is the same thing: a Field with a color input in it. Every fixture has that pair as its twin, and the accessibility tree of the two is the same (CLF-43).
On the web the two members stand in the color field's own shadow root, so the form meets the color field and not the input (CLF-44); focus passes through to the input (CLF-45).

The color is never told by the swatch alone (WCAG 1.4.1), an error is always words (WCAG 3.3.1), and the swatch alone keeps its color in forced colors: each is the color input's or the Field's, and is said there (CLI-25, CLI-35, FLD-7, FLD-17).

web.name: tanrei-color-field
web.notes: The tag `tanrei-color-field`, the class `TanreiColorField`, the React name `ColorField`. The element is composed as every composed element on the web is (the web package's README, Composed elements); what follows is what is particular to it. Members: `<tanrei-field>` holding one `<tanrei-color-input>` in its default slot; the product places none. The host is `display: block`. Value member: `tanrei-color-input`. The host is the form's element — `name`, the value and its state, validity anchored on the input, reset to the `value` attribute, restore, `form`, a disabled fieldset — and the input inside has no `name`. Props, set as properties on the member each is from. On the Field: `label`, `labelHidden`, `supportingText`, `errorText`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `requiredMark`, `requiredText`, `optionalText`. On the color input: `variant`, `size`, `value`, `invalidText`, `picker`, `pickerLabel`. Attributes are the members' own, kebab-case: `label-hidden`, `supporting-text`, `error-text`, `required-mark`, `required-text`, `optional-text`, `invalid-text`, `picker-label`. Props of one name on both members — `label`, `labelHidden`, `error`, `disabled` — are the Field's; the input's are never set by the element and reach the input through the connection. Events: `input`, `change`, `pickerrequest` and `entryerror` are the color input's own composed events and leave by themselves, with the host as their target and `value` already new; `pickerrequest` stays cancelable from outside, and the input reads the result of its own dispatch before it opens the browser's picker. None is stopped and none is copied. Their detail types are the member's, re-exported: `TanreiColorInputPickerRequestDetail`, `TanreiColorInputEntryErrorDetail`. The color input changes a value the product sets without an event — it holds `0F766E` as `#0f766e`, and a text that is not a color as empty (CLI-21) — so the host's `value` is the value member's at every moment, read back changed with no event (CLF-43). Slots: `label-icon` is passed to the Field by a slot element of the same name, rendered only while the host has a child for it. The element has no default slot. Parts: the member hosts are `field` and `color-input`. Exported from the Field: `label`, `label-icon`, `requirement-label`, `supporting-text`. Exported from the color input: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label`, `requirement-label`, `swatch`, `input`, `picker-button`. Two names collide, `label` and `requirement-label`. Each is exported with its member's name before it, always (`field-label`, `color-input-label`, `field-requirement-label`, `color-input-requirement-label`), and under the bare name from both members as well, because the two are one thing to a person and are never drawn at once: FLD-25 is the sentence that holds it. Focus: the shadow root does not delegate. `focus()` and `blur()` call the color input's; a press on the label row focuses the input by FLD-12, a press on the box by CLI-24, and a press on the help does nothing. The browser's picker is opened by the color input from inside its own shadow root, in the user activation of the press on its picker button: two shadow roots deep, which `showPicker()` allows. The connection is the Field's with its control (FLD-25, FLD-26, FLD-28; CLI-43); the element takes no part in it. Parts and tokens of its own: none. The element writes no custom property: `--tanrei-comp-field-*`, `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-color-input-*` reach the members by inheritance, and one color field is set apart by setting any of them on the element. What its twin cannot do that it does: nothing. The twin: `<tanrei-field label="Brand color" required supporting-text="Six hexadecimal digits, like #0f766e."><tanrei-color-input name="brand" value="#0f766e" picker picker-label="Choose color"></tanrei-color-input></tanrei-field>`. Words: the element has none and reads none (CLF-47).

swiftui.name: TanreiColorField
swiftui.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the color input as a view of its own and the color field as the Field around it, reading `comp.input-box`, `comp.color-input` and `comp.field` tokens. `TanreiColorField(_ label:, hex: Binding<String>, showsPicker:, pickerLabel:, onCommit:, onPickerRequest:, onEntryError:)`; `labelHidden` follows the `.labelsHidden()` environment and `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`. The text element, the system color picker and the swatch are the color input's and are in its note. The product's words are read by the Field from the `\.tanreiWords` environment value.

compose.name: TanreiColorField
compose.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the color input as a composable of its own and the color field as the Field around it, reading `comp.input-box`, `comp.color-input` and `comp.field` tokens. Compose idiom, as `TextField`: `TanreiColorField(value, onValueChange, label, …)`; the caller keeps `value` (state hoisting), `enabled` is the inverse flag and `isError` keeps Compose's name. The picker button is shown when `onPickerRequest` is not null. The rest is the color input's and is in its note. The product's words are read by the Field from `LocalTanreiWords`.

flutter.name: TanreiColorField
flutter.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the color input as a widget of its own and the color field as the Field around it, reading `comp.input-box`, `comp.color-input` and `comp.field` tokens. Flutter idiom, as `TextField` and `InputDecoration`: `labelText`, `helperText`, `errorText` and `enabled` keep Flutter's names, `enabled` being the inverse flag. `TanreiColorFormField` wraps it as a `FormField<String>`. The rest is the color input's and is in its note. The product's words are read by the Field from the `TanreiWords` inherited widget.

react-native.name: ColorField
react-native.notes: Not built on this platform yet: the color input as a component of its own and the color field as the Field around it, reading `comp.input-box`, `comp.color-input` and `comp.field` tokens. `<ColorField label="Brand color" value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />`. The rest is the color input's and is in its note. The product's words are read by the Field from the `TanreiWordsProvider` context.
